findings: BLOCKER: InitializationCommit can represent an internally contradictory initialization transaction. It binds commit.review_id to state.review_id and generic review-bearing history items to that same review_id, but if immutable_events contains an InitializationRecord for that review, nothing requires the record to agree with the commit/state on initialization_intent_id, workflow_definition_id, snapshot_id, initial_review_revision, initial_stage, or resulting_lineage_token. A same-review but different initialization record is therefore accepted as part of the initialization commit.

PHASE1_WORKFLOW fixes the canonical ordered five-stage sequence and terminal states; outcome payloads and persistence DTO/protocol signatures reuse the controller-owned domain identity/state types rather than parallel representations; persistence outcomes preserve create/transition retry distinctions. Historical transition data need not equal the current state merely because it belongs to the same review, so that is not treated as a defect in this slice.
